language.name.note: The name of this language in this language, in the list of languages. For German: Deutsch.

language.locale.note: Not a text: the BCP 47 locale for numbers and dates, for example de-DE. en-GB keeps the order day, month, year.

language.label.note: Accessible name of the dropdown of the languages in the header of every page, one word.

language.offline.text: No connection to the server. The page keeps its language.
language.offline.note: Message next to the dropdown of the languages when the server does not answer the change of the language of the account.

language.refused.text: The server did not save the language ({status}).
language.refused.note: Message next to the dropdown of the languages when the server refuses the change without a text of its own. {status} is the HTTP status, for example 400.

language.noStorage.text: This browser cannot keep the choice, because it blocks the storage of this site.
language.noStorage.note: Message next to the dropdown of the languages when the browser blocks its storage, so that it cannot keep the choice.

language.reloadNote.text: Reload the page to show the new language.
language.reloadNote.note: Note next to the dropdown of the languages after a choice. The page keeps the choice at once, but it does not load again by itself, so that a half-filled form stays. The note shows in the chosen language.

language.reload.note: Button in the note next to the dropdown of the languages (language.reloadNote): it loads the page again in the chosen language. One or two words.

start.pageTitle.note: Title of the start page in the browser tab. Skill-Map is the product name.

start.metaDescription.text: Skills as a network of areas, categories, stations and projects. Runs in the browser, the server stores nothing.
start.metaDescription.note: Description of the start page for search engines (meta description). Not shown on the page.

start.tagline.text: Skills as a network of areas, categories, stations and projects
start.tagline.note: Line below the product name in the header of the start page. No full stop.

start.introLabel.note: Small label above the first card of the start page of a plain web space.

start.introTitle.note: Heading of the first card of the start page.

start.introLead.text: The Skill-Map sorts your skills into areas and categories and shows at which stations and in which projects you used them. Readers zoom in and filter by station, project and time range.
start.introLead.note: Lead paragraph of the first card of the start page. Skill-Map is the product name.

start.introStore.note: Bold first sentence of a paragraph of the first card of the start page of a plain web space. The text start.introStoreText follows it.

start.introStoreText.text: Your maps live only in this browser. “Export” saves a map as a file, and “Open map file” brings it back, also on another device.
start.introStoreText.note: Paragraph after the bold sentence start.introStore. “Export” is the button of the map page, “Open map file” the button start.openFile: use the same words.

start.newDefault.text: New map from the default set
start.newDefault.note: Button of the start page: makes a new map in this browser from the default set, a small template of three areas with two categories and two skills each.

start.newEmpty.note: Button of the start page: makes a new empty map in this browser.

start.openFile.note: Button of the start page: opens a map file as a new map of this browser.

start.fileInputLabel.note: Accessible name of the hidden file field behind the button start.openFile.

start.defaultNote.text: The default set brings three areas with two categories each and two skills in each category: software development, data and ways of working. You change them and add stations and projects yourself. The empty map starts without areas.
start.defaultNote.note: Note below the buttons of the first card of the start page. “Default set” is the template of the button start.newDefault.

start.mapsLabel.note: Small label above the card with the maps of this browser.

start.mapsTitle.note: Heading of the card with the maps of this browser.

start.storageWarningTitle.note: Bold first sentence of the warning in the card with the maps of this browser. The text start.storageWarning follows it.

start.storageWarning.text: The browser can lose this storage, for example when you delete site data, in a private window, or when storage runs low. The exported file is the only safe copy. Export your map after each larger change.
start.storageWarning.note: Warning after the bold sentence start.storageWarningTitle.

start.mapListLabel.note: Accessible name of the list of the maps of this browser.

start.mapsEmpty.text: No map in this browser yet. Create a new one or open a map file.
start.mapsEmpty.note: Shows in place of the list when this browser has no map.

start.exampleLabel.note: Small label above the card with the example map.

start.exampleTitle.note: Heading of the card with the example map.

start.exampleOpen.note: Link that opens the example map as a page of its own.

start.exampleNote.text: A click on a skill shows where it was used. Filter under “Projects” and with the time range below the panel.
start.exampleNote.note: Note above the example map. “Projects” is the button of the map page: use the same word.

start.exampleFrameTitle.note: Accessible title of the frame with the example map. Skill-Map is the product name.

site.imprintLink.note: Link in the footer to the legal notice (German: Impressum).

site.privacyLink.note: Link in the footer to the privacy notice.

legal.home.note: Link below the text of the legal notice and of the privacy notice, back to the start page. The arrow is part of the text.

legal.imprintTitle.note: Title of the legal notice in the browser tab. Skill-Map is the product name.

legal.privacyTitle.note: Title of the privacy notice in the browser tab. Skill-Map is the product name.

start.footNote.text: No cookies, no tracking, no other servers.
start.footNote.note: Line in the footer of the start page of a plain web space.

start.licenses.note: Label in the footer before the links to the licenses of D3, of the fonts and of the password check of the account page. Ends with a colon.

start.scriptsMissing.text: The page could not load its scripts. Please reload the page.
start.scriptsMissing.note: Error on the start page when a script of the site is missing.

start.countAreas.note: Part of the line below a map in the list of the maps of this browser. {count} is the number of areas.

start.countGroups.note: Part of the line below a map in the list of the maps of this browser. {count} is the number of categories.

start.countSkills.note: Part of the line below a map in the list of the maps of this browser. {count} is the number of skills.

start.countStations.note: Part of the line below a map in the list of the maps of this browser. {count} is the number of stations.

start.countProjects.note: Part of the line below a map in the list of the maps of this browser. {count} is the number of projects.

site.changed.note: Last part of the line below a map in a list of maps on the start page. {when} is a date and a time, or the text site.noDate. Small first letter.

site.noDate.note: Stands for {when} in site.changed when a map has no date of its last change.

start.damagedTitle.note: Title in the list of the maps of this browser for an entry that cannot be read.

start.damagedMeta.text: The entry cannot be read, only deleted.
start.damagedMeta.note: Line below a damaged entry in the list of the maps of this browser.

site.untitled.note: The title of a map without a title: in the lists of maps, and as the stored title of a new map without one.

start.deleteAsk.text: Delete “{title}” from this browser? Without an exported file, the map is lost then. This cannot be undone.
start.deleteAsk.note: Question before a map of this browser is deleted. {title} is the title of the map.

start.deleteConfirm.note: Button that answers start.deleteAsk and deletes the map.

start.deleteCancel.note: Button that answers start.deleteAsk and keeps the map.

site.mapOpen.note: Button of a map in a list of maps on the start page: opens the map.

site.mapExport.note: Button of a map in a list of maps on the start page: downloads its map file. Use the word of the button “Export” of the map page.

start.upload.note: Button of a map of this browser, for a signed-in visitor: copies the map into the account on the server.

start.delete.note: Button of a map of this browser: asks start.deleteAsk first.

accountCard.private.note: Visibility of a map in the list of the maps of the account, first in the line below the map.

accountCard.link.note: Visibility of a map in the list of the maps of the account: shared with a read link.

accountCard.public.note: Visibility of a map in the list of the maps of the account.

accountCard.linkOn.note: Part of the line below a map of the account, when the map has its read link. Small first letter.

accountCard.linkPaused.note: Part of the line below a private map of the account that has a read link: the link does not work while the map is private. Small first letter.

accountCard.offline.text: No connection to the server. Try again in a moment.
accountCard.offline.note: Error in the account card when the server does not answer.

accountCard.signedOut.text: You are no longer signed in. Reload the page and sign in again.
accountCard.signedOut.note: Error in the account card when the session has ended.

accountCard.refused.note: Error in the account card when the server gives no text of its own. {status} is the HTTP status, for example 400.

accountCard.introLabel.text: Without an account, in the browser
accountCard.introLabel.note: Small label above the first card of the start page on the server, which keeps the maps in the browser.

accountCard.introStore.text: Without an account, the server stores nothing.
accountCard.introStore.note: Bold first sentence of a paragraph of the first card of the start page on the server. The text start.introStoreText follows it.

accountCard.footNote.text: Without an account, no cookies; with an account, only the cookie of the sign-in. No tracking, no other servers.
accountCard.footNote.note: Line in the footer of the start page on the server.

accountCard.label.note: Small label above the account card of the start page.

accountCard.signedOutTitle.note: Heading of the account card for a visitor who is not signed in.

accountCard.signedOutLead.text: With an account, the server stores your maps. You open them on every device and share them: with a read link or in public under your own address.
accountCard.signedOutLead.note: Lead paragraph of the account card for a visitor who is not signed in.

accountCard.signIn.note: Button link of the account card to the sign-in of the account page.

accountCard.register.note: Button link of the account card to the registration of the account page.

accountCard.signedOutNote.text: Without an account, everything works as before: the maps stay in this browser.
accountCard.signedOutNote.note: Note below the buttons of the account card for a visitor who is not signed in.

accountCard.listLabel.note: Accessible name of the list of the maps of the account.

accountCard.empty.text: No map in the account yet. Create a new one, import a map file, or copy a map from this browser.
accountCard.empty.note: Shows in place of the list when the account has no map.

accountCard.fileInputLabel.text: Choose a map file for the account
accountCard.fileInputLabel.note: Accessible name of the hidden file field behind the button accountCard.importFile.

accountCard.signOut.note: Small button in the account card.

accountCard.signedInTitle.note: Heading of the account card for a signed-in visitor.

accountCard.signedInAs.note: Line beside the heading of the account card. {handle} is the user name, in bold.

accountCard.accountLink.note: Link of the account card to the account page.

accountCard.signedInLead.text: The maps live on the server. You open them on every device. In the map, “Share” shares them with a link or in public.
accountCard.signedInLead.note: Paragraph of the account card for a signed-in visitor. “Share” is the button share.open of the map page.

accountCard.newDefault.text: New map from the default set
accountCard.newDefault.note: Button of the account card: makes a new map of the account from the default set.

accountCard.newEmpty.note: Button of the account card: makes a new empty map of the account.

accountCard.importFile.note: Button of the account card: imports a map file as a new map of the account.

accountCard.uploaded.text: “{title}” is now in the account too. The map in this browser stays until you delete it.
accountCard.uploaded.note: Message after start.upload. {title} is the title of the map.

site.noFile.note: Error when a visitor opens or imports a map file without a file.

site.fileTooBig.text: The file is larger than {mb} MB. A map file is much smaller.
site.fileTooBig.note: Error when a map file is too large. {mb} is the limit in megabytes, for example 5.

site.fileUnreadable.text: The file could not be read.
site.fileUnreadable.note: Error when the browser cannot read a map file.

site.alertClose.note: Button of the message box at the top of a map page.

site.invalidName.note: Error when the page writes a document with a bad name. {path} is the collection and the id, for example skills/x.

site.docNotObject.text: A document must be an object.
site.docNotObject.note: Error when the page writes a document that is no JSON object.

local.idRuleAreas.text: small letters, digits, “-” and “_”, a letter first, at most 40 characters
local.idRuleAreas.note: The rule for the id of an area, as {rule} in local.docIdAgainstRule. Small first letter, no full stop.

local.idRuleStations.text: letters, digits, “-” and “_”, a letter first, at most 40 characters, not “{code}” and no small “i” at the end
local.idRuleStations.note: The rule for the id of a station, as {rule} in local.docIdAgainstRule. {code} is the reserved code PRIVAT. Small first letter, no full stop.

local.idRuleGroups.text: small letters, digits, “-” and “_”, at most 120 characters
local.idRuleGroups.note: The rule for the id of a category, as {rule} in local.docIdAgainstRule. Small first letter, no full stop.

local.blocked.text: This browser does not let the page use local storage, for example because site data is blocked. Without it, the page stores no maps. Allow site data for this page, or export your work as a file.
local.blocked.note: Message at the top of a page when the browser blocks its storage.

local.quotaExceeded.text: The storage of this browser is full. The last change is not saved. Export the map as a file, and delete maps that you no longer need.
local.quotaExceeded.note: Message at the top of a map page when the storage of the browser is full.

local.notFound.text: This browser does not have this map. Maybe the site data was deleted. Open your map file to restore it.
local.notFound.note: Message at the top of a map page when this browser does not have the map of its address.

local.damaged.text: The entry of this map in the browser is damaged and cannot be read.
local.damaged.note: Message at the top of a map page when its stored entry is not valid JSON.

local.fileNotJson.text: The file is not valid JSON. A map file comes from “Export”.
local.fileNotJson.note: Error of a bad map file. “Export” is the button of the map page: use the same word.

local.fileNotObject.text: The file holds no JSON object. A map file starts with “{”.
local.fileNotObject.note: Error of a bad map file. The brace in quotes is the first character of a map file.

local.formatMissing.text: This is not a map file: the field “format” is missing, “{format}” is expected.
local.formatMissing.note: Error of a bad map file. “format” is the name of a field of the file. {format} is the format name it-skills-map.

local.formatWrong.text: This is not a map file: the field “format” is “{value}”, “{format}” is expected.
local.formatWrong.note: Error of a bad map file. {value} is the value of the field in the file, {format} the format name it-skills-map.

local.schemaInvalid.text: The field “schema” is missing or is not a whole number from 1.
local.schemaInvalid.note: Error of a bad map file. “schema” is the name of a field of the file.

local.schemaNewer.text: The file has schema {schema}. This page knows schema {max} at most. Reload the page, maybe there is a newer version.
local.schemaNewer.note: Error of a map file from a newer version of the site. {schema} is the schema of the file, {max} the newest schema that the page knows.

local.titleInvalid.text: The field “title” must be a text.
local.titleInvalid.note: Error of a bad map file. “title” is the name of a field of the file.

local.titleHidden.text: The field “title” holds a control character or a broken character.
local.titleHidden.note: Error of a bad map file. “title” is the name of a field of the file. A control character is an invisible sign such as U+0001. A broken character is one half of a UTF-16 pair, which no UTF-8 text holds.

local.collectionsInvalid.text: The field “collections” is missing or is not an object.
local.collectionsInvalid.note: Error of a bad map file. “collections” is the name of a field of the file.

local.collectionNameInvalid.text: The name of the collection “{name}” is not valid. Allowed are small letters, digits, “-” and “_”, a letter first, at most 41 characters.
local.collectionNameInvalid.note: Error of a bad map file. A collection is a group of documents in the file, for example skills. {name} is its name.

local.collectionNotObject.text: The collection “{name}” is not an object of documents.
local.collectionNotObject.note: Error of a bad map file. {name} is the name of the collection.

local.docIdInvalid.text: The document ID “{id}” in “{collection}” is not valid. An ID has 1 to 200 characters and no “/”.
local.docIdInvalid.note: Error of a bad map file. {id} is the id of a document, {collection} the name of its collection.

local.docIdReserved.text: The document ID “{id}” in “{collection}” is not valid. An ID holds no control character and no broken character, and “.”, “..” and “__proto__” are not allowed.
local.docIdReserved.note: Error of a bad map file. {id} is the id of a document, {collection} the name of its collection. “.”, “..” and “__proto__” are ids: keep them. A broken character is one half of a UTF-16 pair.

local.docIdAgainstRule.text: The document ID “{id}” in “{collection}” is not valid. Allowed are {rule}.
local.docIdAgainstRule.note: Error of a bad map file. {id} is the id of a document, {collection} the name of its collection, {rule} one of the texts local.idRuleAreas, local.idRuleStations and local.idRuleGroups.

local.docNotObject.text: The document “{id}” in “{collection}” is not an object.
local.docNotObject.note: Error of a bad map file. {id} is the id of a document, {collection} the name of its collection.

local.docTooDeep.text: The document “{id}” in “{collection}” nests deeper than {max} levels.
local.docTooDeep.note: Error of a bad map file, as the server refuses it. {id} is the id of a document, {collection} the name of its collection, {max} the deepest nesting.

local.docNullCharacter.text: The document “{id}” in “{collection}” holds a null character.
local.docNullCharacter.note: Error of a bad map file, as the server refuses it. {id} is the id of a document, {collection} the name of its collection.

local.docHalfCharacter.text: The document “{id}” in “{collection}” holds half of a character pair.
local.docHalfCharacter.note: Error of a bad map file, as the server refuses it: a lone UTF-16 surrogate. {id} is the id of a document, {collection} the name of its collection.

local.docNotFinite.text: The document “{id}” in “{collection}” holds a number that is too large.
local.docNotFinite.note: Error of a bad map file, as the server refuses it: a number such as 1e999. {id} is the id of a document, {collection} the name of its collection.

local.importedTitle.note: The stored title of a map from a map file without a title.

local.ownerHint.text: The map lives only in this browser. The exported file is its safe copy.
local.ownerHint.note: Sentence on the overview of the owner of a map of this browser, after the hint how to add content.

local.mapPlace.text: lives only in this browser. The exported file is the only safe copy.
local.mapPlace.note: Rest of a sentence on the overview of a map of this browser. The title of the map in quotes comes before it, so it starts with a small letter.

local.homeTitle.text: To the start page with the maps of this browser
local.homeTitle.note: Tooltip of the link to the start page in the header of a map page of this browser.

server.session.text: Your session has ended. The last change is not saved. Sign in again, then you come back here.
server.session.note: Message at the top of a map page when the session of the owner has ended. The link server.signInAgain follows it.

server.offline.text: No connection to the server. The page shows the last state and keeps trying. A change in this time is not saved.
server.offline.note: Message at the top of a map page while the browser has no connection to the server.

server.down.text: The server does not answer right now. The page shows the last state and keeps trying.
server.down.note: Message at the top of a map page when the server answers with an error of its own.

server.conflict.text: Write conflict: this map was changed elsewhere in the meantime, for example in another tab. Your last change is not saved. The page now shows the new state. Make the change again if you need it.
server.conflict.note: Message at the top of a map page when somebody else changed the same document first.

server.limit.text: Limit of the server: {text} The last change is not saved.
server.limit.note: Message at the top of a map page when a write hits a limit of the server. {text} is a sentence with the limit: the text of the server, server.tooLarge or server.tooMany.

server.tooLarge.note: Stands for {text} in server.limit when the server names no limit.

server.tooMany.text: Too many requests. Try again in a moment.
server.tooMany.note: Stands for {text} in server.limit when the server names no limit.

server.notFound.note: Error when the server does not find a map or a document and gives no text of its own.

server.refused.note: Error when the server refuses a right and gives no text of its own.

server.refusedStatus.note: Error when the server refuses a request and gives no text of its own. {status} is the HTTP status, for example 400.

server.goneReader.text: This map is no longer shared, or the link was revoked. The page shows the last state.
server.goneReader.note: Message at the top of the map page of a reader when the map is gone.

server.goneOwner.text: This map no longer exists on the server. Maybe it was deleted in another tab.
server.goneOwner.note: Message at the top of the map page of the owner when the map is gone.

server.missingReader.text: This map does not exist, or it is not shared.
server.missingReader.note: Message at the top of the map page of a reader when the map does not load.

server.noConfig.text: This page shows a map from the server and needs its address. Open the map from the start page.
server.noConfig.note: Message at the top of the map page of the server when it opens without the server. The link server.noConfigLink follows it.

server.signInAgain.note: Link after the message server.session to the sign-in of the account page.

server.readOnly.text: This view may not change the map.
server.readOnly.note: Error when a reader view tries to write.

server.importSignedOut.text: You are no longer signed in. Sign in again, then import the file once more.
server.importSignedOut.note: Error of the import of a map file when the session has ended.

server.notLoaded.text: The map is not loaded yet.
server.notLoaded.note: Error of the export when the map has not loaded yet.

server.startLink.note: Link in the header of the map page of a reader on the server: goes to the start page. One word.

server.readerNote.note: Note in the header of the map page of a reader. {owner} is the user name or the team of the owner.

server.accountLink.note: Link in the header of the map page of the owner to the account page. One word.

server.ownerHint.text: The map lives in your account on the server. Every change is saved at once.
server.ownerHint.note: Sentence on the overview of the owner of a map on the server, after the hint how to add content.

server.mapPlace.text: lives in your account on the server. “Share” shares it for reading, “Export” saves it as a map file.
server.mapPlace.note: Rest of a sentence on the overview of a map on the server. The title of the map in quotes comes before it, so it starts with a small letter. “Share” is share.open, “Export” the button of the map page.

server.homeTitle.text: To the start page with your maps
server.homeTitle.note: Tooltip of the link to the start page in the header of the map page of the owner on the server.

server.noDatabase.text: The message at the top of the page gives the reason.
server.noDatabase.note: Sentence after the notice of the map page that the database does not answer.

share.open.note: Button in the header of the map page of the owner: opens the share dialog. One word.

share.title.note: Heading of the share dialog, one word.

share.loading.note: Shows in the share dialog while it loads.

share.subtitle.note: Line below the heading of the share dialog. {title} is the title of the map, {owner} the user name or the team of the owner.

share.visibilityLegend.note: Legend of the three choices of the visibility in the share dialog.

share.private.note: Choice of the visibility in the share dialog.

share.link.note: Choice of the visibility in the share dialog: readers need a read link.

share.linkHint.text: Whoever has the read link sees the map, also without an account.
share.linkHint.note: Hint below the choice share.link. A map has one read link.

share.public.note: Choice of the visibility in the share dialog.

share.publicHint.text: Everybody sees the map under its public address and with its read link.

share.addressTitle.note: Heading in the share dialog above the public addresses of the map.

share.addressLabel.note: Accessible name of a field with an address in the share dialog.

share.copy.note: Button beside an address or the embed code in the share dialog.

share.copied.note: The button share.copy for a moment after a copy.

share.copyByHand.note: The button share.copy for a moment when the browser does not let the page copy.

share.addressPublic.text: Everybody with the address reads the map.
share.addressPublic.note: Note below the public address of a public map.

share.addressNotPublic.text: Others read the map under this address only when it is public.
share.addressNotPublic.note: Note below the public address of a map that is not public.

share.startLabel.note: Checkbox in the share dialog, below the public address. {address} is the address of the owner, for example https://it-skills.net/anna. There the map shows as the start map of its owner.

share.startHelp.text: Only one map shows there. If you choose this map, it replaces the map before.
share.startHelp.note: Note below share.startLabel while the checkbox is off: an owner has one start map.

share.startShown.note: Note below share.startLabel while the checkbox is on and the map is public. {address} is the address of the owner.

share.startNotPublic.text: While this map is not public, {address} shows the list of the public maps. Without a public map, readers find nothing at that address.
share.startNotPublic.note: Note below share.startLabel while the checkbox is on and the map is private or shared by link. {address} is the address of the owner.

share.linksTitle.note: Heading in the share dialog above the read link of the map. A map has one read link.

share.linkFrom.note: Line below the read link in the share dialog. {date} is the date and time when the link was made.

share.linkPaused.text: The map is private, so the link does not work right now. Choose “With link” or “Public”, then the same link works again.
share.linkPaused.note: Warning below the read link of a private map in the share dialog. “With link” and “Public” are the choices share.link and share.public: use the same words.

share.renew.note: Button below the read link in the share dialog. It asks first (share.renewWarning). Then the link stops working, and a new link takes its place.

share.renewWarning.text: The current link stops working at once, also in frames on other websites. Whoever has it can no longer read the map. Only the new link works, and you share it again.
share.renewWarning.note: Second step after the button share.renew: says what the new link does before it happens.

share.renewConfirm.text: Yes, revoke and generate new link
share.renewConfirm.note: Button of the second step after share.renew: revokes the link and makes a new one.

share.renewCancel.note: Button of the second step after share.renew: keeps the link as it is.

share.renewed.text: New link. The old link no longer works.
share.renewed.note: Shows above the read link after share.renewConfirm.

share.noLink.text: No link yet. A read link lets others read the map, also without an account.
share.noLink.note: Shows in the share dialog in place of the read link when the map has none.

share.create.note: Button in the share dialog that makes the read link of a map without one.

share.close.note: Button at the end of the share dialog.

share.embedTitle.note: Heading of the section of the share dialog that gives the code to show the map on another website.

share.embedPublish.note: Button in the section share.embedTitle: makes the map public.

share.embedCreateLink.note: Button in the section share.embedTitle: makes the read link of the map, which the embed code then uses.

share.embedUseLink.note: Button in the section share.embedTitle of a private map that has a read link: sets the visibility to “With link” (share.link), so that the link works again.

share.embedPrivate.text: A private map cannot be embedded, because only you may see it. Share it, then another website shows it live: in public under its address, or with its read link.
share.embedPrivate.note: Warning in the section share.embedTitle for a private map.

share.embedNeedsLink.text: The map is shared with a link, but it has no link yet. The embed code uses its read link.
share.embedNeedsLink.note: Note in the section share.embedTitle for a map shared with a link that has no read link yet.

share.embedHelp.text: How it works: copy the code into the HTML of your website, for example into your CV or onto the page of your team. The frame always shows the current state of the map: a change shows there after a few seconds, without new code. Readers see the map, the search, the areas and the details of a skill, never your editing.

share.embedColors.note: Label of the choice of the colors of the frame.

share.embedThemeAuto.note: Choice of share.embedColors: the colors follow the system of the reader.

share.embedPanel.note: Label of a checkbox: the frame shows the details of a skill beside the map.

share.embedCodeLabel.note: Accessible name of the field with the embed code.

share.embedPreview.note: Link below the embed code: opens the frame in a new tab.

share.embedOptionsHelp.text: In the code, theme=light or theme=dark sets the colours, and panel=0 shows the details of a skill over the map instead of beside it. In a narrow frame they are always over the map. The mouse wheel scrolls your website, Ctrl and the mouse wheel zoom the map.
share.embedOptionsHelp.note: Help below the embed code. theme=light, theme=dark and panel=0 are code: keep them. Ctrl is the name of the key, as in embed.ctrlKey.

share.embedLinkNote.text: The code holds the read link of the map. Whoever sees your website can read it. If you revoke the link above and generate a new one, the frame no longer shows the map.
share.embedLinkNote.note: Note below the embed code of a map shared with a link.

share.embedAllowLegend.note: Legend of the two choices of the websites that may show the map in a frame.

share.embedAllowAllHint.text: Every website may show the map in a frame.

share.embedAllowOrigins.note: Choice of share.embedAllowLegend: a list of websites follows.

share.embedAllowOriginsHint.text: Other websites show an empty frame instead of the map.

share.embedOriginsHelp.text: One website per line, for example https://example.org. A path does not count: https://example.org/cv allows the whole website https://example.org.
share.embedOriginsHelp.note: Help above the list of the websites that may embed the map. Keep the addresses; the path /cv may take a word of the language.

share.embedOriginsLabel.text: Websites that may embed the map, one per line
share.embedOriginsLabel.note: Accessible name of the field with the list of websites.

share.embedBadOrigin.text: “{entry}” is not the address of a website. An address looks like this: https://example.org.
share.embedBadOrigin.note: Error of the list of websites. {entry} is the wrong entry.

share.embedSave.note: Button below the list of websites.

share.embedOriginsEmpty.text: No website in the list yet: right now no other website may embed the map.
share.embedOriginsEmpty.note: Warning when the list of websites is empty.

embed.openOn.note: Link in the corner of the embed view: opens the full map in a new tab. {site} is the host name of the site, for example example.org, or the text embed.siteFallback.

embed.siteFallback.note: Stands for {site} in embed.openOn when the address of the full map has no host name.

embed.closeDetails.note: Accessible name of the button × that closes the details over the embedded map.

embed.wheelHint.note: Hint over the embedded map after a turn of the mouse wheel. {key} is ⌘ on a Mac, else the text embed.ctrlKey.

embed.ctrlKey.note: The name of the Control key on a keyboard, as {key} in embed.wheelHint.

site.aiLink.note: Link in the footer to the page that explains how an AI tool makes a map from a CV.

ai.pageTitle.text: Make a map with an AI tool · Skill-Map
ai.pageTitle.note: Title of the AI page in the browser tab. Skill-Map is the product name.

ai.heading.text: Make a map with an AI tool

ai.lead.text: An AI tool such as Claude can read your CV and make a Skill-Map for you. You get a map file, or a map that is already loaded in this browser.
ai.lead.note: Introduction under the heading of the AI page. Claude is a product name.

ai.stepsHeading.note: Heading of the list of steps on the AI page.

ai.step1.text: Give your CV to the AI tool.
ai.step1.note: First step on the AI page.

ai.step2.text: Paste the prompt below. The tool reads the description of the format on this site.
ai.step2.note: Second step on the AI page. The prompt is the text below the list.

ai.step3.text: The tool gives you a map file. On the start page, press “Open map file” and pick it. A tool that can use your browser can also load the map for you.
ai.step3.note: Third step on the AI page. The quoted button is the text of start.openFile.

ai.step4.text: Check the map and change it in the editor. The skills and the ratings are the guess of the tool from your CV, so correct what is wrong.
ai.step4.note: Fourth step on the AI page.

ai.promptHeading.note: Heading above the text that the visitor copies into an AI tool.

ai.prompt.text: Make a Skill-Map from my CV. First read {url} and follow the format that it links. Use only what my CV says, rate my skills from its evidence, and tell me what you assumed. Give me the map file, or load it on the site if you can use my browser.
ai.prompt.note: The text that a visitor copies into an AI tool. {url} is the address of the file llms.txt of this site. The AI tool reads the file at this address.

ai.privacyNote.text: Your CV goes only to the AI tool that you use. This site never sees it. The map stays in this browser, and “Export” saves a copy.
ai.privacyNote.note: Note on the AI page about privacy. The quoted button is the text of site.mapExport.

ai.formatLink.text: Description of the format for AI tools
ai.formatLink.note: Link on the AI page to the text file that describes the map file for AI tools.

site.licenseLink.note: Link in the footer to the license of the software (the text file license.txt).
